jobs.occupation: Dynamic flood exposure in Denmark: where will people live when the water comes?
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Environmental Science programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Dynamic flood exposure in Denmark: where will people live when the water comes?

Research area and project description
The overarching aim of this PhD project is to understand how flood exposure in Denmark evolves over time as a result of household location decisions, and to make that dynamic available for cost–benefit analysis of climate adaptation. This is a quantitative PhD: the work combines applied econometrics on Danish register and property-transaction data, a discrete choice experiment, and agent-based simulation modelling. The project is co-financed by the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) and Aarhus University, and the PhD student will be part of the research environments at both institutions.

The project in a nutshell: Cost–benefit analyses of flood adaptation in Denmark evaluate investments over horizons of 80–100 years, yet they treat the spatial distribution of people, buildings and assets as fixed at today's values. Over the coming decades, urban development, demographic change and the gradual repricing of flood risk by insurers, banks and public authorities will reshape who lives in flood-prone areas and what is at risk. At the same time, Danish evidence suggests that flood risk is only weakly reflected in property prices and settlement patterns – households appear to locate under incomplete information about the risk they face. This PhD project treats flood exposure as an emergent outcome of household behavior rather than a fixed physical quantity, and develops an agent-based model of household location decisions under bounded rationality that can project exposure to 2075 under alternative scenarios for institutional risk signals: business as usual, insurance repricing, tighter mortgage lending, and full information.

Qualifications and specific competences
Required qualifications:
• An M.Sc. in economics or spatial data analyses or a closely related quantitative field
• Training in econometrics and experience with R, Python or Stata
• Good written and oral EnglishIt is an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have:
• Experience with panel data, difference-in-differences, hedonic analysis or discrete choice modelling
• Experience with large administrative datasets, e.g. Danmarks Statistik registers
• Experience with or curiosity about agent-based modelling
• Reading proficiency in DanishWe do not expect any candidate to have all of these requirements. The PhD programme includes training in register data, choice experiment design and agent-based modelling, and you will be supervised closely throughout the scholarship. If you have a solid quantitative foundation and are interested in the questions, we encourage you to apply. The role of the PhD student in this project will be particularly focused on the following objectives: 1) a register-based analysis of who lives in flood-prone areas in Denmark and how residential mobility responds to flood events, using Danmarks Statistik microdata linked to building and flood hazard data; 2) a hedonic price analysis of the extent to which flood risk is capitalized in Danish property prices, including event studies around major flood events; 3) a discrete choice experiment estimating how households respond to explicit risk information and to changed signals from insurers, banks and public authorities; and 4) the integration of these results into an agent-based model that simulates exposure trajectories under alternative institutional scenarios and delivers inputs for flood cost–benefit analysis.

The PhD student will enter a research environment with a strong focus on climate adaptation. At the Department of Environmental Science, the student will join the Environmental Social Science and Geography section, which works on environmental valuation, flood damage modelling and the economics of climate adaptation. At DMI, the student will be part of the National Center for Climate Research that produce Danish flood hazard data and climate projections for decision-making at national and municipal levels in Denmark. The student will have office space at both institutions and is expected to take part in the daily research life at both.
You must upload a project description about how you intend to approach the objectives of the project.

Project description (½–4 pages): This document should describe your ideas and research plans for this specific project. If you wish to, you can indicate a URL where further information can be found, but the description should be self-contained.

Qualifications and specific competences: The ideal candidate is highly motivated candidate with an M.Sc. degree with specialization in economics and spatial data analyses, or closely related quantitative fields. Demonstrated oral and written communication skills in English are required. The applicant is expected to present results at international conferences and publish them in international peer-reviewed journals. The applicant should be interested in working in an international and interdisciplinary academic environment. The following qualifications are an advantage, but we do not expect any candidate to have them all:

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Environmental Science, Frederiksborgvej 399, Aarhus University, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Senior Researcher Toke Emil Panduro, e-mail: toke@envs.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Researcher Karsten Arnbjerg Nielsen, e-mail: kan@dmi.dk (co-supervisor)For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk 
How to apply
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 15 November 2026 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 January 2027.

Please make a project description (½-4 pages). The project description should describe your ideas and research plans for this specific project. If you wish to, you can indicate an URL where further information can be found.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via the online recruitment system, which can be accessed under ‘How to apply’.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in RNA Biomarkers and Extracellular Vesicle Biology
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment, Roskilde University, invites applications as post-doctoral fellow in RNA cell biology from April 1st or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Description of the post-doc project
A fully funded postdoc position (18 months) at Roskilde University in the research group of Professor Dalgaard, funded by Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond (Independent Research Fund Denmark) through the project "Enabling RNA Biomarker Origin Detection by Multiplexing Extracellular Tracing". The project will develop a multiplexed extracellular RNA (exRNA)-tracing platform capable of identifying the cell-of-origin of secreted RNAs in plasma and cell media samples and will demonstrate its use by tracing RNA released by pancreatic islet cells and adipose tissue, both highly relevant to type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. The platform will be valuable for validating novel RNA biomarkers and for discovering RNA-based therapeutic targets in metabolic disease.

Responsibilities and tasks
The postdoc’s work will include research within ExRNA biology, RNA biomarker discovery, and multi-omics profiling, with focus on tracing the cellular origin of secreted RNAs relevant to type 2 diabetes and metabolic disease. In addition, some amount of teaching is also required. 

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead the development and validation of a multiplexed exRNA-tracing platform, based on integration of bio-orthogonal proximity labeling and metabolic RNA labeling systems.
• Perform in vitro and in vivo tracing experiments in pancreatic islet cells, adipose cells, and other relevant cell models to determine the cellular origin of secreted extracellular RNAs and extracellular vesicles (EVs).
• Apply proteomics and small RNA sequencing/omics approaches to characterize the RNA and protein cargo of pancreatic islet- and adipose-derived extracellular vesicles and biofluid samples.
• Analyze and validate candidate RNA biomarkers relevant to T2D and metabolic disease, using plasma and other biofluid samples from relevant cohorts or models.
• Mentor younger or graduate students within the focus of the research project.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent within cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, or a related field. Qualifications within the following scientific areas are required:

The ideal candidate has an outstanding track record of accomplishments and a critical mindset. Moreover, an open mentality with focus on research communication, inter-disciplinary curiosity and teamwork will be required to succeed. Moreover, the following qualifications are relevant:

• Certified training in laboratory animal research is required.
• Advanced experimental experience in RNA biology and/or extracellular vesicle (EV) biology is required
• Hands-on experience with proteomics and/or small RNA sequencing or other omics-based biomarker profiling techniques is required.
• Experience with research in metabolic disease, in particular type 2 diabetes or obesity, and/or experience working with pancreatic islets or other metabolically relevant primary cells/tissues, will be highly valuable.
• Experience with publication of original relevant scientific data in peer-reviewed journals will be an advantage.
The ideal candidate should be enterprising and possess good communication skills, be visible and involved in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department and with project collaborators.

Assessment
In the assessment of the candidates, consideration will be given to;

• Experience and qualifications as stated above.
• Academic excellence and scientific production relevant to the description above.
• The ability to promote and utilize research results.
• Experience in mentorship and teaching.
• Ability to communicate in written and spoken English.
• Ability to contribute to development of the department’s internal and external cooperations.
The Department of Science and Environment
Department of Science and Environment is one of four departments at Roskilde University. The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, chemistry, physics, environmental sciences, and mathematics. Bachelor programs are offered within these areas, as are interdisciplinary Master programs. The Department’s laboratories are equipped with modern infrastructure and shared state-of-the art instrumentation. This includes recently acquired NMR, mass spectrometry (LC- and GC-MS, including high-resolution measurements and proteomics), and microscopy (AFM, confocal and fluorescence) instruments, GMO class 1 and 2 labs, flow cytometry, NTA, coulter counter, NGS, Q-PCR facilities, pipetting robots, calorimetry (ITC and DSC), chromatography (HPLC), and scattering (DLS, SAXS) instruments.
The post-doctoral position is within the Section of Molecular and Medical Biology: Molecular and Medical Biology | Roskilde University (ruc.dk)
Read more about the Department of Science and Environment at: https://ruc.dk/en/department-science-and-environment

Questions
For further information about the postdoc, please contact Professor Louise Dalgaard (tel. (+45) 4674 2713) or email: ltd@ruc.dk).

Terms of employment
The position is available from 1/5 2027. The employment is full time, and you will refer to Head of Department Susanne Sørensen.

The position will be filled according to the Agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. 

According to the Pay Transparency Directive, the salary ranges for the various job categories at Roskilde University are listed here. 

Application procedure 
After the deadline for applications the Head of Department will shortlist applicants for assessment with assistance from the recruitment committee including the chairperson of the assessment committee.

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application 
To apply for the position go to www.ruc.dk/en/job/ 

Only applications in English are accepted.

Applications must include:

• Cover letter explaining qualifications, experience and research interests
• CV
• Documentation of education incl. documentation for training in laboratory animal research
• A complete list of publications
• A maximum of 3 relevant scientific works that you want included in the assessment
• If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here).
• Teaching portfolio (read more about teaching portfolio at Roskilde University here) 
If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here)

Material received after this date will not be taken into consideration.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment (DSE), Roskilde University, invites applications for a position as assistant professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management, from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is limited for a period of 4 years.

In announcing the position, DSE looks to strengthen its research in environmental sciences within the following fields: Sustainability transitions and circular economy in institutional and healthcare settings, sociotechnical systems analysis, behavioural and consumption analyses, the economic valuation of environmental and health externalities; and the wellbeing economy as a framework connecting these to the circular transition. The Department is interested in applicants who see large-scale, cross-sectoral shifts of this kind - spanning production and consumption systems - as necessary to address today's pressing environmental challenges across the natural- and social-scientific fields represented in the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The position is closely linked to and partly funded by an Innovation Fund Denmark grant for a newly initiated interdisciplinary research project ROUNDS: Rethinking the cost of care – including the cost of externalities in circular transitions. The project links human health risk assessment, ecological economics, and behavioural research to reduce reliance on single-use plastics and textiles in the healthcare sector.

The Department is interested in applicants whose research and teaching profile includes all the above subject areas in combination with an interest in building interdisciplinary research and collaboration on education. The Assistant Professor’s duties will comprise research at a high international level and a strong commitment and contribution to teaching broadly in the environmental science programs at bachelor’s and master’s level. The Assistant Professor will teach in an interdisciplinary environment and engage in problem-oriented project work with extensive student involvement and responsibility.

DSE is one of four departments at Roskilde University. The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, environmental sciences, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Bachelor and Master programmes are offered within these areas. Research and education within the fields take place in a collaborative and interdisciplinary university environment, also spanning collaboration with the other departments, covering social sciences and humanities, where relevant. The department is organised into four Sections comprising the research and education activities.

The Assistant Professor will be part of the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The Section’s current members primarily have a background within one or more of the fields of aquatic ecology, ecotoxicology, biological production (including aquatic biotechnology), and geochemistry. DSE has a well-established shared infrastructure with state-of-the-art equipment facilities, including field spectroradiometer, Mass-spectrometry (LCMS, GCMS, ICP-MS), CHNS, various microscopy facilities and access to workshops.

Read more about the section at https://ruc.dk/en/research-group/environmental-dynamics

Responsibilities and tasks
The assistant professor’s work will include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication, and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within one or more of the fields of the Assistant Professorship and in general activities at the environmental science programme activities.

In addition to research and research-based teaching, the position also requires sharing knowledge with the rest of society - including participation in public debate. To a limited extent, this may also include performance of other activities.

As assistant professor, you are also expected to complete the educational training program for assistant professors at RUC (up to 220 hours). The training programme will give you pedagogical and didactic tools as well as familiarize you with the Roskilde University educational model called Problem oriented project learning (PPL). Applicants are referred to the university’s Faculty expectations (https://ruc.dk/en/working-roskilde-university ) for specifications on the required level of qualifications within research, teaching, networking, fundraising, impact and outreach etc.

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead and further develop research within the circular economy, sustainability transitions, and environmental management in institutional and healthcare settings, including engagement in the research project ROUNDS
• Develop the field of interdisciplinary research by actively collaborating with other scientific fields within the department or at other departments, connecting environmental science with social science and economics
• Contribute to the development of the research profile of the department
• Maintain a significant record of publications
• Collaborate with colleagues in establishing a vibrant research community
• Participate actively in research networks and external research funding activities
• Teach, supervise, and assess students at BSc and MSc levels. This also implies developing the field in relation to teaching
Qualifications
You must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Science or in the interface between the natural and social sciences applied to environmental and sustainability questions. In addition, a documented qualitative and/or interdisciplinary approach to sustainability transitions is required.

Documented research production at international level within one or more of the following scientific areas are required:

• Circular economy and sustainability transitions in institutional or healthcare settings
• Sociotechnical systems theory and analysis of organisational/infrastructural change
• Valuation of environmental and health externalities, including in relation to public procurement
The ideal candidate has:

• Teaching experience within one or more of the fields of the Associate Professor
• A keen interest and experience in project-based, problem-oriented teaching as well as teaching in an interdisciplinary environment
• Documented experience with interdisciplinary research and interdisciplinary collaborations will also be seen as an advantage.
In addition, it will be seen as an advantage if you can contribute to research and teaching within one or more of these areas:

• Environmental management and monitoring
• Political economy of sustainability transitions
• Health systems and behavioural aspects of circular practice
The ideal candidate must be enterprising, possess good communication skills, and be a visible and involved participant in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department.

At the time of appointment, successful candidates must master English for academic purposes.

Assessment
In the assessment of the candidates, consideration will be given to:

• Relevance of research topic
• Scientific production at an international level
• Research prospective and the ability to promote and utilise research results
• Experience in teaching and education
• Other academic experience, e.g. from organising research conferences or seminars
• Ability to contribute to development of the department’s internal and external cooperation
Questions
Potential applicants from outside Denmark will find information about life in Denmark (taxation, healthcare etc.) at www.lifeindenmark.borger.dk

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Section Kristian Syberg on tel. (+45) 4674 3776 or e-mail: ksyberg@ruc.dk or Head of Department Susanne Sørensen by email: susa@ruc.dk.

Terms of employment
The employment is on full time, 37 hours per week and in the daily work you will refer to Professor Kristian Syberg. Your head of staff will be Head of Department Susanne Sørensen.

The position will be filled according to the Agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Application procedure

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application

Applications must include:

If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here).

jobs.occupation: Growth Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Turn insights into acquisition experiments that scale

**About Good Tape

**At Good Tape, we’re building tools that make working with voice and audio effortless. We help journalists, researchers, and organisations capture, transcribe, and analyse conversations at scale. Our team is small, ambitious, and deeply technical, and we care about reliability and craft.

**The role

**At Good Tape we are ready to level up. We've built up tons of data, a large user base, and a team that's eager to move fast.

We have a world class product, shipping speed and roadmap that warrants our ambition level.

We're looking for someone excited to own Good Tape's acquisition engine: performance marketing, SEO, creative and to fuel our sales motion with a steady flow of qualified demand. You'll report directly to our CCO and work closely with the broader commercial team: Sales, Data, Product Marketing and Customer Success. Your job is to make sure the right people see (and click on) us in the first place, and keep coming back.

It's a rare opportunity; endless data, a real user base and a world class product to market.

**What You'll Do

**Your responsibilities will include:

• Own performance marketing across paid channels, from strategy to execution.

• Drive SEO and organic acquisition, including content and site structure.

• Develop creative strategy and messaging for campaigns and launches.

• Own lifecycle and CRM: nurture flows, retention, and reactivation.

• Own top-of-funnel website content and landing pages; the pages that bring people in.

• Fuel SLG by partnering closely with Sales on positioning, demand gen, and maximizing MQL-to-SQL conversion.

• Feed acquisition learnings into the pricing and positioning conversations led by our CCO.

**What We’re Looking For

**

• A-can-do-mindset who are curious, humble and tech-savvy enough to build manual processes that we can later scale.

• An AI-first approach to problem solving

• Design skills (e.g. static/video ad creative) are a great plus, not a hard requirement

• Proactive, high-ownership mindset with strong cross-functional communication skills.

• Experience in data-driven marketing, growth experimentation, and core SaaS metrics.

• Thrives in a fast-paced startup environment with a proven ability to learn quickly.

**Why join Good Tape?

**

• Work in a small, focused, and highly skilled team where your impact is visible every day.

• Play a key role in shaping our brand, acquisition funnels, and demand gen engine.

• Help define how Good Tape reaches the people who need it.

• Bring passion and proactivity, and see it directly converted into pipeline and growth.

**Apply for the job

**We’re excited to see how you can help us make Good Tape even better for our users.

You are probably studying marketing, communication, business, media or another relevant field, but your specific degree matters less to us than your motivation and approach to the work.

We imagine that you:

• Have a genuine interest in LinkedIn, content and digital communication

• Are curious, proactive and comfortable taking initiative

• Are organized and able to keep track of several activities at once

• Have a good eye for language and engaging communication

• Can work independently while collaborating with colleagues across the organization

Sanos is a clinical development group built around specialized CROs, dedicated clinical research sites and in-house capabilities that support patient recruitment, digital outcomes and clinical supply.

jobs.occupation: Kickstart your Career with Deloitte’s Finance Consultancy Programme
jobs.description:
Are you interested in working in an exciting and challenging consulting role, where you can deploy and develop your skills and competencies within the CFO domain of companies? Do you hold a business-related Master’s degree by the summer of 2027, and are you ready to embark on a life-long learning journey in a leading global consulting firm? If yes, then we might have the perfect opportunity for you!

Who we are

Joining our Finance Consultancy Programme, you will get to collaborate with experienced consultants on a wide variety of assignments and development opportunities. At Deloitte, we work with different project sizes across finance disciplines and industries, but the foundation is always the same: Our genuine passion for the CFO area and creating value together with our clients.

Finance Transformation is part of Deloitte Technology & Transformation (former Consulting) consisting of more than 350 consultants in Denmark who work across all areas of the CFO function. We engage with clients to operate, advise, optimize, and transform their finance functions. Our clients range from domestic to international, from private to public, across various industries, sizes, and time horizons.

You will join a team that emphasizes collaboration, collegiality, coaching, and talent development. At Deloitte, we value diverse skills, experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, encouraging an inclusive and collaborative environment.

Exciting tasks await you

As an Analyst in Deloitte Finance Transformation, you will experience that no workdays are the same. You will face a wide range of tasks, both in the form of interim-based roles and project-based assignments. Projects and tasks will vary across finance disciplines (e.g., operational finance or business finance) and industries (e.g., private or public), and within the first years of your career, you will be assigned to as many different projects and tasks as possible to expand your toolbox and build on your financial craftmanship.

Based on the specific client's needs and your interests, experiences, and competencies, typical assignments and projects could be within the scope of:

• Finance operations optimization and transformation, e.g., controlling, month-end closing, and reporting

• Transformation and digitalization of finance functions, e.g., process optimization, closing excellence, internal controls advisory, and leveraging technology solutions

• Enterprise performance management, e.g., analytics, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting

• ERP-enabled finance transformations and finance systems implementation, e.g., outlining the ERP-strategy, defining business requirements and ensuring consistent data migration

• Finance strategy and operating model, e.g., designing service delivery models, outlining roles and responsibilities and conducting assessments

• M&A readiness and finance post-merger integration

• Global business services transformations, e.g., assessing, developing and implementing shared service functions and aligning service delivery with corporate strategy

• Internal business development and leadership support, e.g., assisting on client proposals, facilitating events and developing material to strengthen our market offerings.

Onboarding and learning

When joining us, you will participate in our onboarding programme designed with the purpose of giving you the best foundation for kickstarting your career in Deloitte. During your first two weeks, you and your peers will attend our Finance Transformation Nordic Bootcamp and our Consultant Academy, where the content is tailored to match your competencies as recent graduates. The Finance Transformation Bootcamp helps you in building your finance craftmanship and toolbox, while the Consultant Academy prepares you for your consulting role in Deloitte Technology & Transformation. Also heavily focused on social activities and team-building, the onboarding programme provides a smooth transition from university as it offers a unique opportunity to connect and build strong relations with your fellow new joiners from day one.

At Deloitte, we believe in life-long learning, and we are committed to investing in your individual development, both professionally and personally, throughout your career. You will experience this with our Finance Consultancy Programme, which is a highly structured learning programme, aimed at equipping you with the appropriate skillset and the right level of competencies needed to succeed in your role.

Leadership and culture

To support your learning, you will also be assigned a People Leader as your closest leader and go-to sparring partner. Your People Leader will help you set the overall direction of your journey in Deloitte and provide guidance across projects to make sure that your individual aspirations and professional development goals are met. Every career path is unique, and together with your People Leader you get the chance to shape your own.

We believe in leadership at all levels, and we have committed ourselves to creating and maintaining an inclusive and psychologically safe culture, where you are encouraged and empowered to take responsibility while leading both yourself and others. We combine this with a substantial focus on continuously staying relevant and being a meaningful social community to our people. We are a people’s business, and therefore we strongly believe that this is an essential prerequisite for making an impact that truly matters – for ourselves and for our clients**.**

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for you, who are passionate about consulting and the CFO-area and who are willing to go the extra mile to deliver sustainable impact that truly matters to our clients. You show an eagerness to make a difference for both clients and colleagues and you are able to see the opportunities and potential in all types of assignments. As our business can be highly changeable, it is important that you are curious by nature, and that you face challenges with an open-minded and solution-oriented approach.

In addition to this, you:

• Have completed a master’s degree within the fields of finance, economics, business, accounting, social sciences, IT, or similar areas in the summer of 2027 or before

• Have achieved academic results from your bachelor’s and master’s degree that you are proud of

• Demonstrate a flair for both oral and written communication and are fluent in English

• Have a legal working permit in Denmark

Although relevant job experience might be an advantage, this is not a requirement.

Want to know more?

Click the "I'm interested"-button above and upload your CV and grade transcripts from your bachelor’s and master’s degree if you are interested and ready to join our team**. Instead of an application letter, we would like you to answer the questions you will be presented with on the next pages** (please only consider the required (*) fields). As we process applications and arrange interviews on an ongoing basis, we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Application deadline: Hiring on an ongoing basis.

Please do not hesitate to contact Giulio Marano (gimarano@deloitte.dk / +45 30 93 64 11) or Maria Banke (mbanke@deloitte.dk / +45 20 97 64 15) if you have any questions about the position.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: Senior Associate, Global Clinical Drug Supply Execution
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

Genmab is searching for an energized Senior Associate to be part of Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery team in Copenhagen within commute distance from our office locations to work according to your hybrid work arrangement.

With an impressive pipeline and many ongoing clinical trials, you will have a central role in supporting inspection readiness across our late-stage clinical development portfolio. Your work will help ensure that documentation is complete, compliant and readily available to support the successful execution of business-critical GMP and GCP inspections.

You will support inspection readiness activities within Global Clinical Supply, collecting, organizing and performing completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation. During inspections, you will participate in back-office activities and help ensure timely retrieval and follow-up of requested information.

The role also offers opportunities to develop beyond inspection readiness. Working closely with Clinical Supply Managers in the Portfolio & Project Delivery team and colleagues across the department, you will support selected operational tasks and initiatives while gaining broader exposure to clinical trial management. Through collaboration with Clinical Trial Operations and CROs, and hands-on involvement in clinical supply activities, you will further develop your GCP and clinical supply knowledge.

The position is based in Copenhagen.

**Responsibilities

**

• Support inspection readiness across late-stage clinical trials by collecting, organizing and maintaining relevant clinical supply documentation.

• Perform completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation against applicable procedures and inspection-readiness expectations.

• Participate in back-office activities during GMP and GCP inspections, including document retrieval, request coordination and tracking of responses and follow-up items.

• Support preparation for mock inspections, audits and health authority inspections, including compilation and review of supporting documentation for completeness and readiness.

• Support activities related to day-to-day trial management, including coordination, follow-up and preparation of relevant material and documentation.

• Support distribution and logistics, including tasks related to shipment documentation, in alignment with the Drug Supply Managers.

• Build knowledge of especially GCP but also GMP and clinical supply activities within Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery function

• Participate in maintenance and continuous improvement of procedures, tools and ways of working supporting inspection readiness and clinical supply activities.

• Responsible for being compliant with Genmab´s quality system.

**Requirements

**

• Minimum a bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

• Some experience working with documentation, quality or compliance activities in the pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical research or another regulated environment is an advantage.

• Knowledge and understanding of GCP and GMP; experience with inspection or audit readiness is an advantage.

• Strong interest in documentation, quality and compliance, with a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work.

• Ability to coordinate activities, maintain structure and follow up on actions involving multiple stakeholders.

• Ability to work successfully under pressure in a fast-paced environment and with tight timelines, including during inspections.

• Ability to be proactive, enthusiastic, curious and goal orientated, with a willingness to learn new GCP/GMP-related activities.

• A team player with demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functional with internal and external stakeholders.

• Strong communication skills in English - both oral and written.

**The Team

**You will be part of a highly competent team focused on end-to-end trial management including planning and maintenance of supplies for clinical trials, working closely with cross-functional stakeholders in both CMC and Clinical Trial Operations.

Together with Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and Global Clinical Supply Systems, the teams make up the Global Clinical Supply department. We foster a supportive, international, and fast-paced work environment centered on collaboration, excellence, and a can-do attitude to achieve results.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK544.000,00---816.000,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

jobs.occupation: Finance Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
Location: On location in Copenhagen, Denmark

Employment type: Full-time

About Teton

Teton is building the autonomous operating system for care. Our technology gives senior living and care teams greater visibility into resident wellbeing, movement, sleep, and care delivery, helping them respond faster, work more efficiently, and provide more personalized care.

The Role

The Finance Systems Engineer will own the systems, data infrastructure, and internal tooling that power Teton’s finance function.

As Teton continues to scale, we need reliable financial data, connected systems, and automated workflows that allow the business to operate efficiently and make informed decisions. You will help strengthen our operational finance capabilities by ensuring our data is accurate, our systems work as intended, and our internal processes are scalable.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of finance, systems engineering, and data. You will build integrations between our accounting platform, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems, develop tools that make business intelligence data easier to access, and establish controls that maintain data integrity.

What You’ll Own

Finance Data and Systems Infrastructure

• 
Own the systems and data flows supporting Teton’s finance function, ensuring financial information is accurate, accessible, and reliable.

• 
Maintain and improve integrations between accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems.

• 
Identify infrastructure gaps and implement scalable solutions that support Teton’s growth.

Systems Integrations and Automation

• 
Build and maintain integrations and automated workflows that reduce manual work across finance and business operations.

• 
Troubleshoot integration issues, resolve data discrepancies, and implement lasting technical solutions.

• 
Identify opportunities to streamline processes through automation and better system design.

Data Integrity and Financial Controls

• 
Develop internal tools and automated checks to identify missing data, inconsistencies, and potential errors across systems.

• 
Establish reliable reconciliation processes and improve the traceability of financial data.

• 
Strengthen data validation and controls to support accurate reporting and dependable financial operations.

Operational Finance Support

• 
Partner with the finance team to improve day-to-day workflows, reporting capabilities, and access to business-critical information.

• 
Translate operational needs into practical technical solutions that reduce administrative overhead.

• 
Build a scalable systems foundation that supports increasingly sophisticated financial and business intelligence needs.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

• 
Built a reliable, scalable finance systems infrastructure with accurate data and strong integrations across accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal platforms.

• 
Automated key workflows and implemented data validation tools that reduce manual work, improve data integrity, and strengthen financial controls.

• 
Improved access to business intelligence and streamlined finance operations to support Teton’s continued growth.

What We’re Looking For

• 
Experience in finance systems, data engineering, business systems, or a similar technical role.

• 
Degree in Finance, Engineering, Analytics, or a related field.

• 
Strong technical skills in integrations, automation, APIs, and data workflows.

• 
Familiarity with accounting platforms, ERP systems, CRM systems, and financial data integrity.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills, ownership, and the ability to work independently in a fast-growing environment.

• 
Experience with finance automation or in a startup/scale-up environment is a plus.

jobs.occupation: Software Engineer(Product)
jobs.description:
About Us

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

The position requires a physical presence at our office in Copenhagen, Denmark. If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.

The Job

We're looking for a talented and driven Product Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build across the whole stack, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Your goal is to shrink the time from a customer request to a deployed solution, without cutting corners on reliability or on the privacy of residents' health data.

In this role, you will focus on:

• 
Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.

• 
Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.

• 
Fast Iteration: Break large designs and features into small shippable pieces. Get MVPs in front of users quickly, measure how they're used, and iterate or kill them.

• 
Backend & APIs: Design and build the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.

• 
Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Build test coverage and use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.

Qualifications

• 
Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build.

• 
Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native.

• 
Comfortable working across the stack: you've built backend APIs and worked with relational databases (e.g. Postgres), not just UI.

• 
Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed.

• 
Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions.

• 
Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team.

Nice to Have

• 
Experience with React Native and Expo in production.

• 
AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience.

• 
Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications.

• 
Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR).

• 
Experience shipping products across multiple markets and languages.

What We Offer

• 
Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

• 
A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.

• 
A Copenhagen-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture.

• 
Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.

At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.

If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.
